audits.decision_reason: All critical checks pass. The mechanism specifies concrete physiological covariates (autonomic tone, vascular compliance, electrode-skin impedance) that induce non-identical conditional distributions, a domain-specific causal path violating exchangeability. Variables are measurable, confounders (genetics, environment, site) are identified, data requirements are clear (multi-subject dataset with covariate-stratified splits), and the prediction (coverage decreases with Wasserstein distance) is testable via the proposed regression plan.

All critical checks pass. Effect size (2-5x variance increase, 15-30pp coverage drop) is plausible per wearable literature. Confounders (sensor type, skin condition, temperature) are identified. The test plan (conditional coverage by SQI bins, adaptive score comparison) is concrete and distinguishes from the physiological-state rival.

The test plan (phase-binned coverage, time-stratified calibration, rival test with night data augmentation) is well-specified.

All critical checks pass. The mechanism identifies a clinical-physiological process: sparse, asynchronous reference measurements (cuff BP, arterial line) with state-dependent triggering (clinical concern) creating heteroscedastic label noise that biases conformal quantile estimation. Variables (reference interval, asynchrony, concern flag) are measurable. Confounders (device drift, clinician bias, movement) are listed. The test plan (replicate-based noise estimation, label-noise-aware score, simulation with oracle predictor) is concrete and distinguishes from model-heteroscedasticity and time-lag rivals.

All critical checks pass. The mechanism specifies pathological subpopulations (HF, sepsis, AFib) with fundamentally altered physiology (e.g., reduced HRV) causing higher prediction error variance, a domain-specific effect modifier. Effect size (3-10x variance ratio, conditional coverage near 0% for high-risk) is large and plausible. Confounders (comorbidity, severity, treatments) are identified. The test plan (conditional coverage by disease label, residual clustering, group-conditional conformal, balanced-calibration rival test) is rigorous and feasible with multi-center data.

The mechanism is domain-generic: the argument that temporal autocorrelation reduces effective sample size (n_eff = n*(1-φ)/(1+φ)), inflating quantile variance and breaking finite-sample coverage, applies identically to any autocorrelated time series (financial, EEG, environmental) without modification. It does not name a specific physiological causal path or boundary condition unique to physiological signals; HRV AR(1) >0.8 is merely an example parameter value, not a domain-specific process. Per the non-generic mechanism rule, this fails mechanism_is_non_generic.

All critical checks pass. The mechanism specifies physiological adaptation processes (medication titration, vascular remodeling) that gradually shift P(Y|X), a domain-specific concept drift source. Effect size (5-15pp coverage degradation per week) is plausible. The test plan (longitudinal coverage tracking, drift-triggered vs fixed recalibration, sensor-replacement rival test) is concrete and distinguishes physiological from sensor drift.

The mechanism is domain-generic: the argument that skewed, heavy-tailed distributions cause symmetric conformal intervals to under-cover in tails and over-cover in the bulk applies identically to any skewed data (financial returns, insurance claims, environmental extremes) without modification. Physiological signals (BP, ICP) are merely cited as examples; the causal path (skewness → symmetric intervals → asymmetric coverage) does not invoke a specific physiological process or boundary condition unique to this domain. Per the non-generic mechanism rule, this fails mechanism_is_non_generic.
